title: Carney government amends controversial bill to fast track pipelines and mines
summary: Liberal MPs agreed to make minor changes to a controversial piece of legislation that's supposed to speed up the approval of major projects.

Liberal MPs agreed to make minor changes to a controversial piece of legislation that's supposed to speed up the approval of major projects.
Liberal MPs agree to minor changes to C-39
Liberal MPs have agreed to make some changes to a controversial piece of government legislation that's supposed to speed up the approval of major projects.

A special House of Commons committee is studying Bill C-39, the Building Canada Strong Act. MPs began going through the massive piece of legislation line-by-line Monday, with committee sitting until midnight. They will resume work on Tuesday morning.

Tucked inside the bill are a dizzying array of more than 300 clauses that amend more than a dozen separate pieces of federal legislation, including laws to protect species at risk, water quality and fisheries. Also inside are proposed changes to the Labour Code, which have upset unions.

blocks.text: Liberals call the legislation one of the most important economic bills in a generation that will enable the federal government to deliver decisions on mines, pipelines and power lines in Ottawa's jurisdiction within one year.
Environmentalists, on the other hand, say the bill guts Canada's environmental safeguards.
Conservatives strengthening guardrails in the bill
Liberals are keeping parts of the the bill largely intact, resisting any major changes the opposition parties are suggesting.

But Conservatives secured an early amendment Monday evening, adding some safeguards and protections around new legislated powers that would allow shovels to hit the ground before an impact assessment takes place.

Typically construction cannot begin on projects like railways and ports, until the environment and climate change minister signs off on an impact assessment review — a thorough evaluation of a proposed project's potential environmental, social, economic and health effects.

blocks.text: Referring to the proposed Alto High speed rail project, Ontario Conservative MP Phil Lawrence said he has heard from constituents concerned about the preliminary work Alto would need to do in his riding.
"There are actions that are being taken with respect to the Alto that may not be reversible at the early stage," he said.

Conservative MPs added language to the bill that would require the review agency to post a copy of any early project work online. In theory, such a notice could enable opponents of a project to challenge in federal court early activities before they begin.
In the eyes of the bill's critics, the proposed amendments may improve transparency and accountability, but they do little to strengthen environmental protections.

"Any amendments being passed right now are small attempts at harm reduction that won't change the balance of harms that the bill proposes," Isabel McMurray, a lawyer with Ecojustice, said Monday night outside the committee hearing.
Ottawa removes blank cheque to approve pipelines
CBC News obtained a copy of the amendments that parties are proposing. The 228 pages of amendments are nearly as long as the bill itself.
National day of action prompts rally in Thunder Bay, Ont., against Bill C-39

Conservatives, the Bloc Québecois, New Democrats and the Green Party are all pushing for changes to the bill that would place more guardrails under the government's ability to designate regions of national interest.

The act gives cabinet powers to designate entire zones as regions of national interest, giving Ottawa broad authority to approve future activities. One example of such an area that could be a candidate is the Ring of Fire, a mineral-rich and ecologically sensitive area of northern Ontario.
Environmentalists have referred to these areas as "sacrifice zones where projects could get rubber stamped."

The Conservatives have submitted amendments that would require more certainty on what kinds of areas could receive the new designation. According to the amendment, the region must contain "existing or reasonably foreseeable development" and contribute to international trade, energy security, critical mineral or national defence.
The Greens want language added to the bill that prevents the government from including existing or future national parks and other protected areas from these zones.
Notably, Liberal MPs are proposing new curbs on the Canada Energy Regulators's powers to approve pipelines without cabinet approval.
When the bill was first tabled in September, Liberals said the bill regulator could approve pipelines on its own that are under 300 kilometres.
But as it stands there is also a clause buried in the bill that gives the pipeline regulator a blank cheque to approve a pipeline of any length without a cabinet approval.
Some Liberals uncomfortable with C-39

The Carney government's willingness to make amendments follow concerns that were raised within the ranks of the Liberal caucus. Two MPs shared their discomfort with the lack of safeguards in the legislation.
Liberal MP speaks out over party's major project fast-tracking legislation C-39
NDP MP Leah Gazan proposed several changes to protect the constitutional rights of Indigenous peoples and to strengthen the language around and free prior and informed consent.
Liberals supported one of those amendments, but rejected most of Gazan's other proposals.

Debate on the C-39 comes as a new report shows federal permitting is rarely a "bottleneck" in getting clean energy projects built. The report cites other factors including "delayed engagement with Indigenous nations, lack of meaningful community involvement."
"We want to see renewable energy projects built from coast to coast at the scale this moment demands," Katie Gibbs, the national policy manager for Climate Action Network Canada, said in a statement.
"But speed doesn’t mean sacrificing environmental safeguards. The sweeping deregulation being pushed through with Bill C-39 will not get projects built faster."
